newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan media give wide play to Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan media give wide play to Deng's death.

text.p: Taiwan's media on Thursday gave extensive coverage to the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, focusing on his political career and the possible impact on China's relations with Taiwan.

Most Taiwan newspapers ran banner headlines, while state radio and television aired virtually non-stop broadcasts of Deng's death and invited scholars to analyse the potential impact on Taiwan-China ties.
Many newspapers said the death of the Chinese patriarch on Wednesday should not affect near-term cross-strait relations.
In its editorial, the mass-circulation China Times newspaper called on Deng's successors to follow the paramount leader's policy of peaceful re-unification between Taiwan and China.
"His successors should maintain peace (with Taiwan) and assist in Taiwan's development under the principles of relaxation, exchanges, mutual help and fraternity," the paper said.

But the mass-circulation United Daily News said despite the economic reforms initiated by Deng, the paramount leader was reluctant to "let go of his socialist policy". It also accused Deng of allowing the military to fire at pro-democracy supporters during demonstrations centred on Beijing's Tiananmen Square on June 4, 1989.

The newspaper called on Chinese authorities to transform their economic reforms into political reform, but urged local pro-independence activists to refrain from provoking China in the wake of Deng's death.
Taiwan and China split after a civil war ended in 1949, but Beijing still views the island as a renegade province subject to eventual unification.
It has threatened to retake the island by force if Taipei tries to declare independence.
